## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Xíng yuàn pǐn shū chāo* in 6 fascicles combines [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) Chéngguān's separate-circulation commentary on the *Pǔxián xíngyuàn pǐn* 普賢行願品 (cf. [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041)) — a more compact version than the 10-fascicle [X227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0069) — with [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) Zōngmì's accompanying sub-commentary (*chāo* 鈔). The two works circulated together as the standard late-Tang apparatus for the *Pǔxián xíngyuàn pǐn*, paralleling the much larger *[Shū-Chāo](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011)* format that Chéngguān had pioneered for the parent *Avataṃsaka*.

**Abstract**

The work is conventionally datable to the period 820 – 841 CE, the bracket of [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) Zōngmì's mature scholarly activity. The *Bié xíng shū* of Chéngguān is a separate, more concise commentary distinct from the 10-fascicle [X227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0069); Zōngmì's accompanying *chāo* extends the commentary in pañjikā format. Together the two works constituted the standard late-Tang apparatus for the *Pǔxián xíngyuàn pǐn*, and were used in East Asian devotional and scholastic practice from the late ninth century onwards.

The work is preserved in the Manji *Xù zàng jīng* (X229) collection.
